title: What to Do When the Definition of Small Business Changes
summary: SBA's proposed size standard increases could reclassify 114,541 companies as small overnight. Here's what capture and BD teams should do before the rule is final.
body_markdown:
AI has freed up time that proposal and capture teams used to spend on busywork. Now might be exactly the moment you need it, because a shift is coming that's going to reward whoever thinks it through first.


The[SBA](https://www.goveagle.com/govcon-glossary/sba-small-business-administration) is proposing to raise its[size standards](https://www.goveagle.com/govcon-glossary/size-standard) for[NAICS](https://www.goveagle.com/govcon-glossary/naics-north-american-industry-classification-system) categories, in some cases significantly:


- Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services (541611) goes from $24.5M to $295M.
- Custom Computer Programming Services (541511) increases from $34M to $531M.


Those are just six of the 338 NAICS categories in the proposal. If it goes through as written, 114,541 established companies will be reclassified as small overnight. Check the[full Federal Register notice](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-20/pdf/2026-17042.pdf) for how every other code you compete under is changing.


## Every Government Contractor Has a Stake in This


An SBA small business designation touches every contractor differently, but nobody is unaffected.


Large businesses may find far more work set aside, as the small business pool grows to include highly capable firms. Small companies operating under the current standard could see competition increase radically. Mid-sized operations, over today's threshold but under the new one, may end up best positioned of all, but the landscape they compete in won't look like the past.


Things get stranger from there. Expect top-tier primes to pursue[Mentor-Protégé relationships](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/large-prime-mentor-protege-teaming-strategy) with newly "small" half-billion-dollar firms, and joint ventures to form between organizations that are enormous in every sense except the legal one.


The agencies and NAICS categories you've focused on may become crowded battlegrounds, while ones you've ignored could turn attractive. Your list of competitors is about to need an update.


## Get in Front of It While Requirements Are Still Being Written


[RFIs](https://www.goveagle.com/govcon-glossary/rfi-request-for-information) and[Sources Sought notices](https://www.goveagle.com/govcon-glossary/ssn-sources-sought-notice) carry more weight right now than usual. They're your chance to shape how agencies write requirements before the new size standards reshape who's bidding against you.


Teaming, competitive intelligence, and proposal volume may all need a different approach going forward. Are your processes up to the challenge? Does your capture need better intelligence? Are you using AI for maximum benefit? Change is in the air, and now's the time to get ready.


## The Comment Period Closes September 21, 2026


Whichever seat you're in, prime, small, or newly in the sweet spot, this is the window where your input can still shape the final rule instead of just reacting to it.


Submit comments through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at regulations.gov, referencing RIN 3245-AI67 or Docket No. SBA-2026-0199, or mail them directly to SBA's Office of Government Contracting and Business Development.


Pro Tip


If you're a GovEagle customer, ask GovEagle's AI chat to help you draft your comment for the docket.


## Re-Score Your Pipeline Before the Final Rule Lands


Look at your pipeline with new eyes. Every bid/no-bid decision you made under the old size standards was made with old information, and some of those calls will change once 114,541 companies are reclassified at once.


Start the relationships now: Mentor-Protégé conversations, JV structuring, deciding who you want teamed with in a world where "small" might not mean what it used to. No tool builds those relationships for you, but knowing who to have those conversations with, and having that list update itself as the landscape shifts, is exactly the kind of thing capture intelligence should handle automatically instead of living in someone's head.


There's also analysis you can move on today: re-scoring your pipeline, re-running competitive intelligence on who might get added to your weight class, and watching the agencies and[NAICS codes](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/govcon-set-asides-guide-small-businesses) you'd written off in case they open back up. This is where speed compounds. Firms that re-map their pipeline in week one have a real head start over the ones still working off the old picture in month three.

Continuous monitoring watches your competitive landscape and this rulemaking for you, so nothing slips through because someone forgot to check. Bid/no-bid analysis that took days now takes minutes, so a reclassification affecting 114,541 companies doesn't mean weeks of manual re-scoring.

Put together, that's the difference between scrambling to react and moving with confidence: faster bid decisions, a cleaner pipeline, sharper[P-Win](https://www.goveagle.com/govcon-glossary/pwin-probability-of-win) , and pursuits worth your team's time, without the all-nighters a shock like this usually forces.


The size standards will settle into a final rule eventually. The businesses that come out ahead won't be the ones who worked hardest to keep up. They'll be the ones whose pipeline, competitive intelligence, and proposal engine were already built to absorb this kind of change without missing a beat.
